It focuses heavily on acquisition strategies and how firms have done deals in the past, as well as what kind of deal pitfalls are commonly seen. Highly, highly recommend!!
Great professor and class, good to take for personal knowledge/even though not going into consulting/asset management

So good!!! Should be considered in the next tier out from a core class. Amazing professor (one of the best at Marshall) who is exceptional at delivering very complex subject matter very understandably, without it feeling over-simplified. Take this.

He is tough but very fair

We should be learning the tools of today's real estate finance corporations, and we should be evaluating and understanding the project financing that's going on today.

Class is taught by Rook and I think he's retiring after this semester - but overall the class is a bit fluffy, but I think I'm learning more about the importance of qualitative research and could probably run a focus group now so I guess that is valuable.
Outdated professor

Extremely useful insight into.. as the title suggests, consumer behavior. Useful for product managers, entrepreneurships, strategy and of course marketers striving to figure out how to appeal to their market segments.

This class should be a 1.5 unit based on the current content. It feels like an undergraduate class and could be sped up significantly. There is a straight-forward midterm and final and a larger consumer journey mapping project which should not be bad to complete. There is significant overlap between this class and New Product Development.
I think Professor Folkes in fantastic. We have a small class, which may no be the case in future semesters, and have fun class discussions.

Gulden is great, and passionate about consumer behavior as it is her area of expertise. The class content is interesting and helps you to understand how people think and make decisions (which can be useful for many career functions). We've also had some great guest speakers so far. Some overlapping content with the core marketing class for those who took it with Gulden. Overall a pretty easy but interesting class.

This semester's class was completely online and all exams were open-book, open-note (not sure if this will be the case in the future). Gulden is extremely organized and stays on track with her lecture slides. Most of the information is pretty straightforward, but overall a pretty interesting class that should be an easy pass.

The notes and learnings for every class are extremely organized. Pretty minimal workload - there are a few short papers and one group project. The midterm was open book and I imagine the final will be as well. Gulden is an excellent professor and very passionate about the topic.
Relevant content. Kristin has great energy. All assignments and readings are highly insightful.
Chill af. I breathe a sigh of relief in this class knowing that I can daydream for all of class and still ace every assignment.
Boring

This class has a very easy workload and the content is easy to grasp. I would say that overall we have not covered too much content (I wish we would learn some more honestly) but the things we have covered can definitely be applied in a marketing or entrepreneurship career.
This class is a lot of work but interesting. Good guest speakers and fun in class exercises

Professor Badama is super passionate and a great teacher. The guest speakers are fun and we do interesting activities in the class that make it enjoyable. There is a fair amount of work however, so just know that going in!

As someone who struggles with Marketing concepts, this class is incredibly informative and Prof. Badame does a great job of bridging concepts together. In-class exercises are interesting and guest speakers are fantastic. It is a lot of work though, so please plan accordingly with your schedule, but overall really manageable!
Professor is not good and too much work, would be better class with different professor

A lot of work writing wise, some individual and group assignments, there is a midterm, the final is a group presentaiton - overall she is easy going and an easy grader - she does expect you to attend class
This class seemed very interesting at first but the things we talk about is so general, seems like undergrad things. Nothing new learned here and the assignments are pretty useless

there is a lot of busy work in this class/small assignments that feel unnecessary but the big portions of your grade are two midterms and a group project
Who is this class for? great for anyone interested in CPG
Final Thoughts: Professor Diehl brings in great guest speakers
I am not focusing on marketing so this class was not the most useful. But Professor Ulkumen is great, and I could see this being a valuable class to the marketing oriented folks.
Not very insightful. Great class if you want light workload and need to fit your schedule.
Light workload, pretty easy exam. Professor is a little dry and the stuff taught is pretty basic.
Repeat of a lot of what we learned in core, teacher doesn't explain concepts well, either.

comments: This class is just OLD. Many of the advertisement examples are over ten years old. Some of the cases are interesting but the discussion led by the professor is so slow and basic literally no critical thinking is involved. There were very few FT MBA students in the course. There is a lot of busy work for class and he covers many concepts. Tellis is nice as a person but it is not a worthwhile class.
topic_title: MKT 526 - Advertising and Social Media Strategy

comments: Not the best class, but I think it is a must for marketers.
topic_title: MKT 526 - Advertising and Social Media Strategy

comments: A lot of the information feels old and outdated. He doesn't keep up to date with the latest trends and just gives a high level outline of what has been done in the past. You don't learn how to create effective advertising.
topic_title: MKT 526 - Advertising and Social Media Strategy

comments: The lectures are just a summary of the reading, so no real value add to come to class. The project was interesting but was poorly explained as the professor is unclear with directions often.
topic_title: MKT 526 - Advertising and Social Media Strategy

comments: Tellis is an accomplished speaker and researcher. He keeps the content fairly simple but it is still helpful to spend more time going through and can be applied in a variety of industries. There are a number of mini assignments but they are not too hard and he drops the lowest couple. The midterm is a presentation. The final is short and the main semester project is analyzing and remaking an ad. One downside is this class does not really cover social media - it is more about advertising as a whole. Class was small and he facilities good discussion and includes good cases. He is also hilarious and very open to helping students.
topic_title: MKT 526 - Advertising and Social Media Strategy

comments: The professor Steve Martin is very arrogant and full of himself. The book he wrote is the basis of his class, and he wants his students to memorize every term he made up and concept he named as if it was gospel. I found this to be a class where obvious, known concepts we have all already learned in intro psychology, communication and marketing courses were given new names with a sales bent. We learned a few interesting things, but not enough to make this a useful full semester course.
topic_title: MKT 528 - Sales Management: The Art of Science of Sales

comments: This is a really good class for someone who feels they need professional development or needs to learn how to better market themselves. The tenants he teaches however, are directly from his book and if you read the book you don't necessarily need to take the class. It's an OK class. This is not a class you left your job for. This is not a class that is going to alter the course of your career.
topic_title: MKT 528 - Sales Management: The Art of Science of Sales

comments: Professor is good and the course is useful. Could have been a half course as mostly let out an hour early. Not a lot of work. Useful skills but lecturer does not post his slides or record lectures or have available time to reach him. So hopefully you remember everything from the class (although tests are all based on his book which is ok).
topic_title: MKT 528 - Sales Management: The Art of Science of Sales

comments: Professor is not humble, but a nice guy. The class is super helpful for people who are still recruiting, even if you don't want to go into sales. It helps with interviewing, stepping outside of your comfort zone... and the class isn't too difficult.
topic_title: MKT 528 - Sales Management: The Art of Science of Sales

comments: Could go either way, started out strong but really faltered halfway through. If you need it to get you out of your comfort zone to "sell yourself", then take it.
topic_title: MKT 528 - Sales Management: The Art of Science of Sales

comments: Pretty overrated class. Professor moves at a quick pace, so be prepared to catch up if you can't keep up. A lot of the concepts are too helicopter to be truly applied in a real world business sense. Lots of group work, expect to be doing a lot with your groups. Siddarth is entertaining, but the class most of the times is not.
As currently structured, this should be a 1.5 unit class.

Skip this class. Professor has never launched a true product in his life. True example of: "Those who can, do. Those who can't, teach". He gives stories about his past experience rather than anything of substance. Far too much work for what little you learn. You'll be doing a ton of work with your group so make sure you pick a good group.
Is a good course for those interested in CPG marketing. Not sure how useful it'll be for others.

"Dr. Rook is a really good guy. He likes to talk, he's funny, but not the best teacher. He can hold your attention for the whole class easy which is good, but I never felt like i was learning a ton.

The reader he makes you buy is really good. Expensive, but a lot can be learned if you planning on doing the readings.

4 homework assignments (long and tedious)
1-2 mini projects

1- Do I want to buy a course reader that costs $160?

Useful to learn more about all the steps leading to the launch of a new product.

Such a terrible waste of time and money. Prof is nice and funny and means well but this class could be supplemented by buying the course reader and watching a random assortment of Tosh.O videos while drinking and you'd probably learn more. He clearly is not in tune with todays world and doesn't care to catch up. Most questions are answered with speculation or straight up disinterest and he never cares to follow up and learn about what he didn't know how to answer. Two thumbs down
Professor Rook is entertaining and the class is always fun. The readings are helpful and relevant to the course.

The professor it is not engaging and uses a lot of old cases and examples. However, the main project makes you go through all the process of developing and launching a new product, which makes you learn and it is interesting.
The class discussions are less structured than others and not as valuable.
The material is OLD, needs to be updated with new stuff. I understand the Prof is mainly going on his experiences but maybe consider bringing guest speakers for stuff more relevant today.
Just OK. Not an incredibly structured class (which could be viewed as a benefit considering the material), but the project is a bit pointless, and most of the material is common sense..

Excellent course reader - but that's the limit. DOn't take the class, just buy the reader. Prof is checked out - classes are more him telling stories of funny stuff that happened to him than any insightful new product teachings. Assignments are "busy work", no real learning or insight. Avoid.

Rook is funny, engaging, and has a great sense of humor. Yes, some of his material is a little dated, and he even brought a VHS in to class once, but it's a solid class and Rook is a solid professor. There is some reading and written homework, two relatively easy midterm/quizzes, one small group project, and one big group project. Overall, his class is more than worth your tuition money and you will be stimulated, engaged, and amused for the class if you show up and care. I look forward to taking more classes with Rook!
This course is not structured well and feels very "fluffy". Although important concepts are mentioned, we don't delve into any deeper or critical points.

Given my career and passion for brand management, I was really excited to learn more about NPD. Unfortunately, this class has been a huge disappointment. Professor Rook has no structure to his lectures. He rambles on and on about personal stories and anecdotes that teach you nothing. His lecture slides look like they were made from the 1980s and some of the marketing challenges and examples are literally from the 1980s. He refuses to update the content this class, which is very frustrating. If you're taking in the course, the best thing you can do is just show up, listen to what he has to say, and hope you learn and thing or two from it.

NPD is great for marketing. Professor Rook is very animated and amusing so class goes by pretty fast. There are a lot of short stories and anecdotes that Rook shares in a class so there's not much note taking, but his tests ley heavily on the readings and concepts, so be sure to be on top of them. / The project is pretty fun and open for creativity. there are a few simple deliverables during the semester (mostly ungraded) on which Rook gives guidance and feedback.
Learn some useful frameworks and theories, but for the most part everything I know I learned on the job.

A few long papers and three group projects make it above average work load. Class provides good exposure to the fundamentals of the stage gate model (idea to launch), but provides little beyond an introduction to the concept and some basic, well-known real world examples (like analyzing why Segway was a failure, etc.). A good intro (slide shows mostly photos of ad campaigns), but wish it was more in depth.

Do not take this class. Learned no new information from other marketing class. Professor Rook, while funny, makes fairly inappropriate jokes. The whole class is story time for his career in advertising mixed with offensive jokes. Complete waste of time.
The examples used are pretty out of date and the class ends early more often than not.  I'm not really sure I've learned anything new that I didn't get from the core marketing class.

Excellent class, excellent professor. Thursday nights can be rough, but if you have any intention on ever being a part of a new product launch, it is worth it. This is also an excellent class to take if you're interested in branding - it is way better and more relevant to MBAs than Sasha's branding strategy class.

I swore I'd never take a Thursday night class again, but I'm so glad I took this one. The professor is really engaging and how I wish more professors would be - great lecture slides, great at facilitating discussions, great at explaining concepts in an easily understandable way. It is a case-based class and there are surveys due the day before, which can sometimes take a while if there are calculations. TBD on how the main group project will turn out since we're moving online, but would highly recommend this class for anyone going into marketing.

This is one of the best classes I've taken at Marshall. The professor is fantastic at facilitating case discussions and at bringing in real world examples from his work into the lectures. He's also the only professor I've had that's successfully integrated the final project into his classes - for example we brainstormed concept ideas for the final project in the first class. I'd highly recommend this class for anyone who's interested in marketing or enterpreneurship.

If you are pursuing Marketing as a career, you have to take at least 1 Badame class while you are at Marshall. She cares a lot about her students, puts in the effort to bring in excellent guest speakers, and provides great frameworks. None of her classes are fluff classes though - there is a lot of work and case readings. I would also say (now that I've taken 2 different Badame classes) that they are very similar, so if you take one you're good

Badame is a great professor - she puts in so much effort into her classes, bringing in multiple great guest speakers and making sure content/cases are relevant and fresh. The project/case write up are a lot of work, but she is very organized and helpful.

VERY discussion heavy. The class is long and the first half is only discussion where everyone has their hand up for the whole period. Second half is guest speakers sometimes or meetings for a group project. He then has lecture videos posted where you teach yourself the content for the assignments not in class. Definetly a good guy and means well, but not a lot of of information shared for the projects or assignments so have to teach yourself.

Class is entirely case based. Cases are generally interesting and present a diverse set of strategies, problems, founders, etc. Overall the workload is managable. This class is NOT an incubator to launch a new product or workshop a new business idea, as one might presume from the title. Professor could do a better job of moderating class discussions. There are some valuable hard skills that can be learned from this class, such as sizing a market and caculating a break-even point, but the Prof spends no time teaching this and expects you to watch his pre-recorded lecture videos on your own time or do supplemental readings.

The class is very organized, and covers interesting topics. The first half of the class is a review of the case (in a battle of attrition to get called on through a sea of hands), and the second half is lecture. Larry has amazing experience, and his stories add a ton of value. I wish Larry would spend more time talking about examples from his rich work history. Students come to class very prepared, because there is a poll about the case before each class. Larry is actively teaching students to NOT think critically, but I still believe the class is a really good one. The project itself is pretty unorganized, but could be fun if you are committed.

As others have mentioned this class is very heavily case-based, which I wasn't expecting. The cases and discussions get old after a while. I wish there was more hands-on exposure to NPD through the group project. The project feels pretty rushed and like we aren't really gaining experience through it. Larry is great and super knowledgable. He occasionally presents real world case examples that he's done, which I wish there was more of. Also guest speakers so far have not been super interesting.

I love Larry and I think he's great. He is one of the few Professors at Marshall that are extremely engaging and from whom you'll learn a lot. The cases are really interesting as well. BUT, as much as I love him and would recommend his class, he gives you a LOT of busy work that we could have gone without. The workload for this class feels like a 6 unit course, which should be adjusted for next year. So, overall, if you can, you should take this class because it's one of the few classes you'll actually learn a lot, but expect to be BUSY.

Very relevant topics ranging from market sizing, break-even analysis, qualitative research, design thinking, learning from extreme customers, segmentation and targeting, brand strategy, prototyping, and more. It's a lot of work but worthwhile work that gets you thinking. The class itself can feel stressful at times because everyone is trying to get participation points. This was all online and with 70 or so students it's just not possible to hear from everyone each time. Communication is a bit all over the place: slack, blackboard, emails... I wish there was just one platform we used instead of seaching all over.
One of the best classes I've taken here. If you want to do Product Management this is the class to take. Professor is amazing and the content is amazing!
Professor is amazing. It's a totally case-based class so be prepared for discussing and even debating! You'll learn a lot and the optional readings are really valuable.

Great class and great professor who may also be a work-in-progress. The class is a lot of work, but is an incredible learning opportunity. The prof has a background in both marketing and finance so he teaches lots of market sizing, forecasting, etc. Marketing meets finance meets product. If you take this class, be mindful of your workload in other classes as well. This class is probably best paired with classes that teach complementary material.

The best course I have taken at Marshall so far, it's so relevant to the skillsets I need. The professor is very knowledgeable and puts a lot of efforts. The course is very heavy on cases/assignments. There is a submission before every class, and a group project aspect too. The class discussions are very interesting, and he follows the case discussions with his own learning material every class.

Amazing professor, but the class is okay, it felt like an extension of the marketing core class. I wish the professor focused more on go-to-market/actually launching the product vs focusing mostly on the beginning process/customer needs.
Heavy homework, a lot of indivisual assignments along with group project. Professor goes with a quite slow pace. not recommended for MBA students

I find class materials interesting. You need to spend a lot of time on individual assignments and group project. Some people think the lectures are boring, but you learn a lot from lectures and assignments/project.
Who is this class for? New Product Development is not really optimized for tech product development - most useful for students interested in CPG

Regarding Course Workload -- there are both individual assignments and group assignments. If the assignments felt more directly tied to learning product development, I would find more value and motivation in completing them. The individual assignments involve a lot of work, but they haven't felt particularly effective in helping us learn how to do product development. For group assignment, we have to develop a new product by the end of semester, which feels more aligned with practical learning and has been relatively more useful. 

Regarding Grading Toughness -- my rating has more to do with the lack of clarity in the grading criteria. For example, in Individual Assignment #1, we were instructed to use AI to generate a list of 20 product successes and 20 product failures. Then, we were asked to use our own thinking to discuss which product succeeded/failed. The professor deducted major points when he thought I used AI to answer the analysis/self-thinking part of the question. 

While resubmission is an option, I'm not really sure what I can change regarding the analysis/self-thinking part of the answers as it is my own analysis to begin with. It is unclear what criteria the professor uses to determine whether AI was used or not. For example, I use double dashes "--" in my writing style, and I wonder if that was the reason he chose to believe AI was involved in the analysis/self-thinking portion. This lack of transparency makes it difficult to understand expectations and frustrating to have to rewrite my own words/thinking and resubmit assignments in order to receive a higher grade. 

Additionally, for the questions where the professor want us to use AI, he asks us to highlight the outputs in red, and paste the prompts in blue. If you prompted AI to give you "one paragraph of the list without description," instead of giving the whole list where there is a "title + description of the title," he also deducts point on it. 

With another AI-based assignment coming up, I still don't feel confident in how to meet the grading expectations. If there are strong concerns about AI use, it might be worth reconsidering whether AI-focused assignments are the best fit, or at least providing clearer guidelines on how the assignments will be evaluated to begin with. I wish that the lack of grading clarity in Schorr's class was something clear in previous elective surveys. I would have taken into consideration before selecting a class with unclear grading criteria.
Who is this class for? If you are interested in CPG. This class is not great for tech. 
Final Thoughts: If you are interested in CPG, I suggest taking this class with another professor if possible. Otherwise, you may find more value in other product-related electives. Beyond the grading concerns, it is worth noting that classroom expectations are quite strict. For instance, if you arrive 15-20 minutes late, the professor may pull you aside and question you about your tardiness. This didn't happen to me peresonally, but I observed it happen with several classmates. 

If you miss a class, you are required to submit mutliple pages of memo to demonstrate that you have watched the lecture recording. You are to type out answers of class discussions on the memo and write out five takeaways from each class. 

In class, you will be expected to engage in discussion via: traditional participation (raising hands and answering questions), Slack, and collaborating with your group via Google Doc during class (which can be done through traditional participation in class).

All of these are experiences to be aware of in advance as they shape the classroom experience.

The course material is extremely relevant and interesting but the amount of work for this class can be quite overwhelming some times.
Who is this class for? Anyone interested in learning how to properly develop new products from research through launch.
Final Thoughts: The class is very informative but it does have a very slow pace and this professor assigns quite a lot of homework and projects.
This course focuses mainly on one single approach to branding strategy, but remains interesting to learn how to create brand attachment.

"A very holistic approach to Branding. I haven't learned a ton from the class, but it's a very easy A-/B+ and I learned something.

1 Midterm (easy)
1 Take-home assignment (short and easy)
1 Final (probably easy)

I'd still 3 it for a class to take. The reader is pretty good, and the professor is a really good guy. If he can't answer a question on the spot, he makes it a point to research and come back to it the next class."
Class is too slow and easy. Not an MBA level course. Not a high ROI class. Professor is nice but he moves way too slowly. Impossible to stay focused because of this. Would NOT 3 this to anyone.
Very helpful
Badame has amazing guest speakers, and a similar format across her courses.

Dr. Badame brings in relevant speakers who are currently working in branding at organizations from a variety of industries. There is quite a bit of coursework involved for a half semester class and sometimes the assignments are a little unclear. However, she structures the class well and there is usually a lot of participation involved. It's a good class for anyone trying to go into brand management. She has great connections too so it'd be a good idea to get on her good side.

This is one of the most intense 1.5 unit classes I have taken at Marshall. The amount of reading and work that she assigned was for a 3 unit course and she crams it all into a 1.5 unit class, which really doesn't help with learning the material. I really wanted to dive deep into marketing but I would never take another class with this professor, she is a difficult grader and there is A LOT of reading, cold calling, etc. Take at your own risk!

Easy course, interesting cases, and speakers. Fairly easy workload. Badame uses the same class structure for all of her classes, so if you;ve taken a class with her before, it's the same deal. Case studies in class, open book midterm, group project, individual case write up, and 2 single-page reflection papers on the guest speakers.

If Professor Strauss is teaching then definitely take this course.  Very manageable workload, only 2 major projects and a few quizzes.  Class is very entertaining and Sasha is the best.  You will not want to miss a class unless you absolutely have to.

Easily the best marketing class I have taken thus far at USC. Prof. Strauss' presentation skills rival Patton's, and possibly exceed his. (Strauss does TED talks, which may go some way towards explaining his abilities.)    And, due to the fact that he runs his own brand consultancy, he has access to a wealth of real-world case studies that you won't get access to anywhere else.

I strongly recommend taking this class wiTh this professor, I have heard the same class with other professors is not good.
Sasha provides real life examples of his consulting firm projects and a very practical approach to branding problems.

Great professor with plenty of real life examples that one can apply. / Great guest speakers. / Very engaging and motivating. / The professor is also really interested in students and offers time for one on one meetings to speak about career and personal projects regarding brands. / Really useful and actionable learning.

The best non-quantitative marketing professor at USC who knows his stuff and keeps up-to-date with the trends in brand strategy.  Runs his own firm and has a lot of great insight.  A must take if you are a marketing student for the professor alone.
Should probably be a 1.5 credit, but nevertheless an amazing class
This was my favorite class this semester!  Sasha has such a great perspective and I am very excited that I was able to have him as a professor.

This is hands down THE BEST COURSE I HAVE EVER TAKEN. Professor Strauss is a marketing legend. He is very quirky and animated in the way he teaches, but it keeps you really engaged and you get used to his style pretty quickly. He often talks about current marketing and branding problems real companies are having right now, so you know everything he discusses is very relevant. His teaching style is the perfect balance between conceptual knowledge and real world application. Strauss is the CEO of his own brand strategy agency, and I love that he uses case studies of his actual clients. He even brings in some of his employees as guest presenters, and they are all fantastic. If you have even the slightest interest in marketing, I highly encourage you to take this course. I guarantee you won't regret it.
Engaging professor. Worthwhile to attend class.

I took this course to brush up on marketing since Core. It is A LOT of work for a 1.5 unit class--two 5+ page papers and a presentation (think 30 page deck). The course material is quite repetitive as well and I think dated for marketing.

Interesting case studies in the class, but I feel like too much was crammed in for a 1.5 unit class. I liked how she incorporated the readings with the lectures and there were a few great guest speakers. She expects a lot in terms of assignments and readings, be prepared.

Professor Strauss provided great examples and added good variety to the class. He brought in great guest speakers. The group project was super helpful to analyze all aspects of a brand and provide recommendations for the positioning statement, etc.

Wish it was a little more structured. Think there was good information to pull out, but sometimes the class felt scattered and not structured to get point across. 

I do think a lot of the things he talks about are relatively common sense. 

That being said, I like the real-life problems.
Sasha is very passionate and gives great lectures. Perhaps he had too many guest speakers come in. Having a little more theory would be great as well.

Best marketing class in Marshall! The professor runs an agency himself so he has many real cases to talk about. He really cares about students. Besides teaching the branding strategies, he provides many advices on career development as well. Highly recommended!

Very fluffy class. Some interesting lectures but for the most part its common sense material. Not a lot of work at all ('pop' quizzes, solo project and group project). I think this course taught by Sasha would be better served as a 1.5 unit class.

BEST PROFESSOR EVER! This is why I came to Marshall - for professors and classes like this. Professor Strauss is a genius, is an expert in Brand Strategy, cares deeply about his students and UNDERSTANDS us, and is one of the most engaging speakers (He's done TED talks and presented to Google). He will use time to explain career paths and compensation for agency side and client side of brand strategy/marketing because he knows we'll be looking for jobs. He brings in recent brand consulting examples from his own company and more because we need to see what's happening now - not 5 years ago like all other Marshall marketing professors. Only take brand strategy with this teacher - not Badame. I really hope Marshall sets their marketing standards higher to match classes and talent like Professor Strauss.

I don't understand why the class has such a great peer evaluation last semester. I bid for 800 points... The professor is nice, but the class is... hum... the professor is teaching the very very very basic stuff on class... for example, the different customer services which you can read a book within 20min but he can talk for a week... a waste of time... but very very very few homework... So, if you want to enjoy a good California lifestyle or you want to focus on more career.. take the class.

This class is incredibly high-level. My biggest complaint is that we talk at the 50,000-foot level every week and rarely get down to a tactical, meaningful level. The speakers that have come into class have been marginally useful. I think there are better courses out there for your money, unless you're just looking to be entertained. Sasha is a good presenter and is engaging, but I do not think the value was there for this class.

Much of the information in this class is very intuitive, so the class can feel a bit pointless at times. However, the professor provides very interesting examples of marketing strategies in companies that have been both successful and unsuccessful. The professor is engaging and fun.

I have mixed feelings about this course. The project is asinine. The professor teaches like a Sunday preacher. Terrible shoes. Bt it does provide a lot of insight into the process behind developing a brand. Probably more interesting if you want to work for an ad agency or something.

An incredible amount of reading every class, especially for 1.5 unit course. 30-40 pages each class. Not very practical and speakers are hit or miss. Concepts are interesting but the class format is not ideal.
Just okay. A lot of material and was covered quickly/superficially. I didn't feel like I learned very much over the term. Speakers were okay, but not amazing.
Not necessarily helpful for finance, but does a fantastic job of reviewing all the decisions involved within marketing
Decent class, but Strauss is so passionate he makes it entertaining.

Sasha is a great professor. He is very engaging and enthusiastic about the material. There are occasional quizzes and few course deliverables. He brings in guest lectures almost every week. Highly recommend if you are at all interested in marketing/brand management.

Branding strategy is not separated from strategy. The professor brings high profile consultants and experts almost every class as guest speakers. Super applicable stuff for anyone wanting marketing or Strategy

There are some interesting topics here for discussion, but the class is so mundane and repetitive that everyone uses this class as a study hall. Prof is terrible at engaging the class and relies on outdated videos on branding strategy as frameworks. It might just be that is was on Zoom, but in the virtual setting, I would not recommend this class at all. It is all over the place and I have a hard time even listening to the professor. It might also be that my expectations were high...if yours are low, perhaps this is a good fit for you. If you are decent at Excel, this class will move slow for you at times. The class is centered around group projects where the data fits perfectly. They can all be accomplished by just following what he did in class and using his formulas in your Excel file. In reality, the world doesn't work that way so I struggle to think that this class is going to be super applicable to my marketing career.
topic_title: MKT 543 - Market Demand and Sales Forecasting

comments: It will be really be up to you if you want this class to help you in the future. Its easy to just memorize things for the class and not understand how to apply them, altough the professor really tries to.
topic_title: MKT 543 - Market Demand and Sales Forecasting

comments: Funny and lively professor is also compassionate to students who are less advanced in using data.
topic_title: MKT 543 - Market Demand and Sales Forecasting

comments:
Good professor with good content. The professor also has a sense of humor, which made the 3 hr class not feel that long. 
Assignments are very much related to what he teaches in class and if you are paying attention in class, not a lot to prep for the 
exams as well. Fair exam as well. If you want a good sales forecasting class, this is the one for  you

exams as well. Fair exam as well. If you want a good sales forecasting class, this is the one for  you
topic_title: MKT 543 - Market Demand and Sales Forecasting

comments: The professor is pretty funny, calls everyone in the class Boss. A lot of examples seem to focus on CPG, but concepts are extendable to most marketing applications.
topic_title: MKT 543 - Market Demand and Sales Forecasting

comments: The class provides very interesting quantitative tools for market research, sales forecasting and marketing in general. It is the most interesting class I have taken. The professor is very approachable and involved with the class. He is always open to answering questions or clarifying the models in detail - this helps because the course concepts are really heavy. Coursework is also quite heavy but it is a value adding must-have course at Marshall.
topic_title: MKT 543 - Market Demand and Sales Forecasting

comments: Group assignments do a good job of testing you on the material for the course. Exam was fair.
topic_title: MKT 543 - Market Demand and Sales Forecasting

comments: Professor Siddarth cares about his students and keeps class entertaining. The models he has taught are definitely helpful to know, but probably would help more people interested in pursuing a career in marketing. That being said, I am learning models and tactics I have not learned before and expanding my Excel skillset in the process.
topic_title: MKT 543 - Market Demand and Sales Forecasting

comments: Professor Siddarth has a lot of energy and engages the class well. A lot of marketing analysis tools are thrown at you, so the hope is that some of these will stick and translate in the real world.
topic_title: MKT 543 - Market Demand and Sales Forecasting

comments: Essential content for any marketing professional, but the professor is not good at teaching. Cons: While I agree with other reviewers that he has a great sense of humor, he does a poor job of guiding the class. I often find he goes on tangents, and goes too fast on some difficult concepts and too slow on easy things. Mainly, I Prof. Sid. is not good at providing structure to the class, so I often get lost on how details matter for the bigger picture of the topics we are discussing. I found the assignments to be long and medium-difficulty, and the way he phrases questions makes it hard to understand what he is really asking for. I also don't like that 40% of the grade is the final exam (especially in a class where a lot of the work is excel-based). Pros: the conent of this class is VERY relevant to anyone going into marketing, and I would even say for anyone going into a field that touches marketing (consulting, strategy, etc.) I took the class because I knew the content was very important, but due to the poor teaching I found myself lost during class and teaching myself a lot of the concepts independently. To excel in this class, you should feel comfortable in excel and not be intimidated by regression, otherwise you will be overwhelmed.
topic_title: MKT 543 - Market Demand and Sales Forecasting

comments: Siddarth's class is frustrating, lectures can be incoherent at times and the homework is very challenging even if you attend every class session. However, if you're interested in marketing, confident with doing regressions or know how to use JUMP,  and like fast paced teaching styles you will benefit from taking this class.
topic_title: MKT 543 - Market Demand and Sales Forecasting

comments: Prof. Siddarth is chaos contained. If you are well versed in excel/regression/math formulas within excel then I reccommend. I also reccomend if you are serious about marketing and understanding adoption, forecasting demand, conjoint analysis, promotions, CLV, etc. The professor teaches JMP for a lecture or two - but allows you to use it on assignments so if you understand it, it will come in handy running regressions, semi-log and log-log (if what I just wrote causes you heartburn dont take this class). Overall very useful class, somehwat long and in-depth group homework assignments, no midterm, and a final worth 40% of your grade. Take the class with a group of friends and make your own group so you can commisserate together while trying to digest what Prof Siddarth said in between "Hey Boss" Also do not skip - he will call you out every time you come back (unless you really dont care, but good luck teaching yourself from his slides)
topic_title: MKT 543 - Market Demand and Sales Forecasting

comments: I believe this was the first time this class was taught to grad students. The professor has previously taught it to undergrads. Maybe it's partially because grad students didn't have a lot of prior experience with Figma, but the class felt pretty disorganized, and we don't build a lot of technical skills. There is a semesterlong project for a real-world client. The individual assignments and exams are very easy.
topic_title: MKT 551 - From Strategy to Execution: User Experience (UX) and Design

comments: Relevant material for tech-focused business people, but certainly could be taught much better. Prof seems quite disorganized, but the assignment structure is relatively rigorous (graded on completion for most part). Limited teaching of actual real life tools like Figma even though we are expected to understand how to use them. Midterm requires some studying, but should be relatively easy to learn.
topic_title: MKT 551 - From Strategy to Execution: User Experience (UX) and Design

comments: I do think this is super useful information, especially if you're heading into tech. I think the class lectures/discussions are a bit messy, but still some interesting takeaways.
topic_title: MKT 551 - From Strategy to Execution: User Experience (UX) and Design

comments: the prof is very nice and helps the students a lot. focus on more technical skills like figma would have been better. the prof sometimes loses track of the slides but is overall very knowledgeable
topic_title: MKT 551 - From Strategy to Execution: User Experience (UX) and Design

comments: Nice class, nice professor. It is not too much work and a useful class if looking for a half course to do. Depends on what else you have done though as to whether you well get more additional value out of this, but not too bad.

Take this class if you want an easy class. Pretty low on work required, and the professor is a nice guy. You won't learn too much, but you also don't need to attend all of the classes or apply a lot of effort. One large group project due at the end of the semester.

The class was vague. Although there were a lot of case studies, they were not well linked to concepts, and concepts themselves were not laid out very clearly. The class is pretty low impact, so if you need something easy, this would be a good option.

Class is very simple, but important. You learn about how to keep your brand consistent across complicated value chains. Professor is very experienced and applies a lot of real-world examples into lessons. Gary is also quite a goof...always cracks jokes [some not so funny, but in a way that makes them even more funny!]. Very easy class with minimal work as well.

This class is easy, but also not stimulating or of much value. The ideas in marketing channels are vaguely interesting, and perhaps taught by a different professor could be of more value, but Professor Fraizer's style is not worth the your MBA tuition fees.

Professor might be a little behind the times on marketing strategy, but he is open minded and willinging to learn just as much from you are you are from him. He is incredibly caring for his students. The cases are pretty cool and the class discussions were usually fun.

Great class, but Fraizer essentially just talks about cases he works on and his career. It ended up being a very broad class. There were just 2 tests that consist of 4 questions and you pick 2 to answer in essay format. Overall, it was very straight forward.

This class approaches the process of setting a distribution network for a company or product, identifying the best option between direct and indirect sales and the possible consequences of switching between these two options. It is about how you make your distribution more efficient and not so much about how you communicate the benefits of a product through different channels. The professor is a very nice and experienced person with plenty of examples of past consulting projects with companies that range from Apple and Intel to CocaCola China and Triumph.
Very little homework. Not much new material/concepts were covered, classes were based on socratic method where we voiced our opinions on various issues.

Light workload - there are no case readings except for the final project case. Midterm is straightforward and professor is relaxed. Class was mostly discussions around handouts on different topics. If you go to class and follow the discussions you'll get more out of the class.

I find this class to be an extremely useful survey of the marketing landscape across all industries. Class time is extremely dialog-heavy without much emphasis on lecture material; I find this method to be extremely useful, but it's not for everybody. Gary has a ton of experience in marketing and consulting and I loved hearing his thoughts on the companies and projects he's worked on. Don't expect to be challenged as you may in some other Marketing classes, but this is a great survey-type class if you're not focused on Marketing for a career but still want an overview of what's going on in that space.

Very traditional. He does a lot of subtle boasting about his successful career, high paychecks, and wealthy wife. Also, all "cases" he writes up himself are based on his personal experience as a marketing consultant 30 years ago and does not know anything about digital marketing or social media.
It was largely a waste of time though the cases were interesting. The professor is a well connected guy but thought to listen to for the duration of class.

This professor has been teaching this class too long and has not updated the material. He's a nice guy but freely admits he doesn't know much about ecommerce and therefore doesn't teach much about it. It's a very light workload if you're looking to balance your classes but there aren't a lot of tangible takeaways

Professor Frazier made changes to the class after previous feedback to be more cased based. He covers 10 cases throughout the course and they are all quite interesting. He only takes your top 4 grades though, and is a very generous grader. He is also really funny in class, and makes it a very enjoyable experience. Additionally, the content is also valuable, and does a great job discussing how channel strategy plays into greater strategy overall.
Class is unique and helps develop thinking in sales and distribution. Coursework is light and professor is engaging and funny. Definitely a useful class for marketers.
Great professor who is nearing retirement. If you are looking for a course with a light workload, this is it. Talks a lot about how marketing and sales interact across industries.

This class focuses on product distribution and supply chains, and isn't very relevant for anyone whose job function is going to be primarily digital. He admits that he doesn't know much about social media, digital marketing, or e-commerce. If your industry has physical product distribution, this could be a very valuable class. Regardless, the workload is light and the grading is fairly easy, and the professor is nice and funny.

The worst class I've taken in my academic career. Gary maintains a high standard for his students' deliverables. Unfortunately, this standard is not reflected in his own material. The content is outdated and the lectures are disjointed and unorganized. Gary often asks questions but has no additional insights to share and sometimes does not know the answer himself. The takeaways from the case readings, beyond the obvious, are non-existent. If your name is remotely ethnic, Gary will butcher its pronunciation and may ask you to change it to something else. While classes are 80 minutes long the content could easily be explained in half the time. This became readily apparent after our first online session which lasted ~35 minutes. Laptops are not allowed in class.

Gary is the worst professor I've had at Marshall. He relies on his prior work career for class examples, which are irrelevant in how society and marketing have evolved over the last two decades. He did not know what an Amazon locker was, which, as a supposed marketing professional and professor is unacceptable. Furthermore, his knowledge on topics related to marketing are lacking -- when anyone asks a question (and he asks for questions constantly), he seems to talk around the question and never actually answer it. He is a self-professed "white guy from Minnesota" who refuses to pronounce anyone's name that is not a stereotypically white name.

Worst corse that I've taken at Marshall. The professor's knowledge are outdated, as well as his ability to use technology. The lecture is poorly structured around the consulting projects he worked for his clients from 10+ years ago. Doesn't know how to sharescreen on zoom, doesn't know how to post grades on blackboard... Not learning anything from this corse.

The course materials are decent but delivery is not great. It's an easy course to take if you are interested to learn about sales and distribution channels. The professor is aged and very monotonous, but he has a lot of experience. Coursework is light.

The information is pretty straightforward and applicable across industries (centers around distribution channels and salesforces). You can tell that Gary has a lot of great professional experience, but I wouldn't say that he's the best teacher. Most classes end early, coursework is very light (you choose 4 out of 8 or so cases to write 1-page recommendations) and the exams are fair. He cares about his students, but teaching seems to be something that keeps him busy post-retirement and he's more interested in getting to know students.

Professor Weiss is knowledge about the subject which is rapidly evolving. Workload is minimal - No readings, no homework, 2 quizzes, and a final project. You will get nothing from the course if you don't go to class sessions because that is all there is.
Very useful class and different from other marketing class

this class is really very generic and did not give me any thing solid about internet marketing. Most of the concepts discussed in the class were quite familiar to me through general knowledge about the social media and the kind of tools being used by companies today. The class does not go into actual implementation of internet marketing in a real life scenario - we do not actually understand how to perform search engine optimization in practice. this course would be best offered as a 1.5 credit rather than a 3 credit one.

Weiss is laid back, funny, and smart. I found that I already knew a lot of the content in this class from my previous professional experience, but still found great value in his class and would highly 3 it to anyone who will deal in the digital space in their career - which, is probably most people. He's approachable, the class is interesting, and EASY. There is absolutely no reading, two small quiz/midterms, and one final group project.
Have to go to class, but workload is minimal. Some interesting topics.
A MUST!!!! No syllabus or readings = go to every class and pay attention will pay off
Professor is really nice. Don't feel like this class is adding to my education

Not very useful. Talks a lot of fluff about how google algorithm works and how 'Big Data' is changing marketing. But nothing specific or useful. You'd be better off watching a Ted talk on digital marketing/

Half of the course is mostly introduction to Digital Marketing which is not helpful if you have been following it up in news and observing trends. The course until now has not been useful in becoming better at internet marketing. More practical application needs to be implemented in course learning.

"Really unorganized class. About 1 month left in the class and we don't have a syllabus or really know what he wants with our final class project.

No homework
2 Midterms (hard)
Final Project

This class might be A LITTLE helpful for people looking to go into digital marketing for their internship or after school. But overall, I did not like it or look forward to coming to class."

The content is super useful and practical. Most of those materials are up-to-date and really help me a lot for my job hunting as well. The professor taught the class in a very easy-to-understand way. Yet, the midterm was slightly way to hard. This class is highly 3ed to everyone who is interested in any job related to Internet or digital marketing.

Class takes a comprehensive look at the digital media space. If you have no background in marketing or digital media, this is a great class to take. If you know about social media marketing or SEO then you might not learn a lot. The group project is a real-life consulting project where you can apply what you're learning, so that is a pretty valuable project.

You're probably thinking "I know everything about social media, SEO, etc." You don't, Professor Weiss is very knowledgable on both marketing, but also the technology behind everything. No reading, just need to show up in class making it a very straight forward class. Professor Weiss is very funny and keeps the class entertaining. Worth taking if interested in marketing.

If you are into digital marketing, this is a great class. Professor Weiss is extremely experienced and very smart. / He brings a lot of his own experience to the class and the material is very useful. / A lot of the concepts do get pretty technical though, so if you don't have a tech background, or you are not interested in learning more tech things, it might be a bot harder for you to follow. / The project is a bit vague at first and is pretty independent (no deliverabels during the semsmter, just final hand in - no presentation)

Prof. Weiss is a current practitioner, due to his leadership of his company Marketing Profs. His information is up to date, and his explanations are very clear. A great class for any aspiring marketer.

It is a very basic class, and I felt that a lot of it I ended up knowing simply because I use social media. Weiss does offer a new perspective and even explains html and introduces a lot of vocab. There are 2 short answer tests and in order to get a good grade on them, you really do have to be going to class or have some good notes. There is also a course long project, where we essentially consult for an actual company. Overall, it can be dry at points, but there is some good information if you are getting into digital marketing.
I really like that there's a real life hands-on project for the course. It's a great place to apply everything we've learned.

A great background for anyone wanting to know more about marketing on the Internet.  This course provides a detailed overview on each concept.  Should have been offered in conjunction with Intro to Marketing.
This lecture-based course was sometimes slow, but covered very up-to-date material. Definitely useful for my internship. Aside from the final group project, very little work outside of class.

Although I'm not pursuing a career in Marketing, I have taken multiple Marketing classes that I feel are helpful for anyone. This has not been the same case for me. Evaluations are not hard.

The class is dry although topics are somewhat interesting. He brings around 4 guest speaker and provides real-life consulting project in which you can provide recommendations about how to improve the digital marketing strategy of the company (even getting access to the company's google adwords account which I find very interesting).

Everything is going digital. This class was super helpful in giving a high level overview of digital marketing and how to approach KPIs, email marketing, etc. I even used a lot of it during my summer internship!

He is knowledgeable. But goes off on tangents. A lot of disinterested students surfing the web. Many students don't show up to class. Seems like it is tough to get good grades. Exams are all short answer type..no MCQ.

I took this class so that one day I could start my own website/business or at least understand the latest buzz regards digital marketing/strategies. Unfortunately, this class failed to deliver that other than giving a brief skeleton structure about what's out there. I learned more through YouTube videos and Googling the terminology and concepts introduced in the class. The actual delivery of the content could be immensely improved by the professor. If anything, this course feels like an undergraduate course where you would be memorizing terms for the midterms rather than critical thinking skills and application of the content for a business.

Lots of useful information in this class, especially for those not familiar with the topic. The professor is clearly smart and knowledgeable, but has trouble synthesizing information and presenting it in an interesting way.

Course materials could be better organized. Professor are confusing sometimes. Python workshops are dry. We lost a lot of time with in-class exercises that lack approapriate preparation/background. Do not take this class.

Professor Nikhil is commited in the sense that he regurly tries to bring updates in his curriculum and include what is the new tech which is aiding or disrupting digital marketing space. His selection of guest speakers is great in the sense that it covers to what he teaches in the class and beyond.  This is much more than just SEO, SEM where in you can get the knowledge of how digital media strategy is used to boost top line of the company.
You can learn a lot about digital marketing. Not everything the Professor teaches is on class slides, so you need to pay attention in class if you want to do well in exams.

The class content is very interesting and relevant to any marketer. The first half of the class goes deep into analyzing the numbers and the overall data science behind digital campaigns and can feel a little complicated for some people.
Who is this class for? Marketers trying to better understand how the digital marketing world functions and operates.
Final Thoughts: The professor is highly knowledgeable, and another instructor—who teaches some of the lectures—brings extensive experience from working with a variety of successful brands. Together, they create a strong synergy between academic theory and real-world strategy.
It's Badame so we all know what that means - a little all over the place but good frameworks and great case studies and speakers. Good class especially if you need marketing connections 2nd semester!
A lot of great speakers. Learned a few new interesting marketing frameworks. A good choice for marketers.

Once you've taken one of Professor Badame's classes, you've taken them all. That's because she structures every one of her classes the exact same. The only difference is the case studies you are required to read. However, she's still a good professor overall. She really cares about teaching you important marketing concepts and she puts in a lot of effort to prepare for each class session. But above all, her ability to bring in amazing guest speakers is her greatest strength.
Badame has amazing guest speakers, and a similar format across her courses.
Cases are fairly diverse and interesting. As a night class, the last hour can be hard to get through, but it's just once a week.

A really good marketing strategy class. Marketing strategy is very similar to business development and strategy, so if you liked strategy courses this is a good one. There is a lot of reading to be prepared for and the speakers are all pretty good. The articles in the course reader are also very useful to reference if you are doing consulting or any marketing policy.  The professor is enthusiastic about the class.

If you're interested in marketing, this class is a must take. Professor Bedame is mediocre, however she brings in a ton of very successful, and engaging speakers. I think we had 9 speakers this semester from companies like EA, Toyota, Yahoo!, etc. This course is what our intro marketing class should have been, case based learnings similar to Corp Strat but with a marketing focus.

This class had a lot of potential I thought but it's awful.  there is no structure to it and he doesn't actually teach anything.  It's all based on a simulation and he doesn't give any guidance to actually educate you so it becomes just arbitrary decisions.  there are readings assigned also and you have to come  up with BS questions about them (these are graded) and a group is assigned to present on the reading you just read and no one pays attention.  Can't over emphasize what a waste of time this one is.  Also he doesn't hold office hours and I've emailed him twice and neither time have I gotten a response in less than 2 weeks.  Seriously.

This class has been such a disaster. So disorganized, so much random work. The speakers have been great and the professor is so nice and passionate, but the overall course needs a lot of work before it's worth taking.

I really enjoyed the focus on current cases and interesting/relevant companies such as Uber, Snapchat and Trader Joe's. The lineup of guest speakers was excellent. The class focused more on strategy than marketing.
Badame gives somewhat frameworks. Her passion in marketing shows and she's able to bring in amazing guest speakers. Not the best marketing class but helpful to take if you're interested in marketing.
Great speakers, not too much work (one individual paper, one midterm, 2 reflection papers, one group project that reports twice)

Badame is a classic experience and her strongest quality is her ability to bring in amazing guest speakers. Actual course material in terms of content is so-so. Much of it feels repetitive. You can balance your workload pretty nicely though.
Badame brings amazing guest speakers to class. I highly recommend this class for anyone pursuing marketing as a career function.
The content is great and dense, great speakers, useful frameworks, but the class is too fast.

A great class to get Badame's hot take on general marketing strategy. Amazing guest speakers. This is my first and last class with Badame, however. She is lovely and encourages participation and peer learning, but the coursework is just too much. Definitely recommend taking only one class of her's.
Badame is great and truly cares about the subject and her students. It is a lot of work but manageable.
Amazing, engaging class with great speakers and a highly intellectyal and engaging professor
This is a super easy class. It's a bit of work with lots of cases and readings but the Prof. Badame has a really good course structure. It's definitely worth taking at least one of her classes.

Badame has a TON of energy, she brings in really great guest speakers, and she brings a wealth of knowledge to the table. Some of the cases are a little outdated, but this class is a really great deep dive into strategic marketing frameworks. The group project is a big lift, but because you can split it between a group of 5-6 it makes it manageable.

The professor asked you to purchase the Markstrat simulation and work with your team on the simulation for the whole course. 
Who is this class for? 
Final Thoughts: I didn't like this course by this professor at all because it was a waste of time and money. The course workload was light, and the professor was easy too, but you won't learn so much because he only taught for a few sessions and dedicated the rest of the class for teamwork on the simulation.

Who is this class for? Marketing/Consulting interest
Final Thoughts:

Who is this class for? Good class to take if you're interested in marketing. It's like too high-level/easy if you already have a background in marketing.
Final Thoughts: Prof Silver is GREAT. Such an engaging teacher. However, the course content might be too high-level/easy if you already have a background in marketing.

career: Consulting | Additionally Supply Chain and Operations
comments:
Who is this class for? Most useful for marketing and consulting 
Final Thoughts: I love how the class explorers the concepts and how the professor explains these concepts. The professor is very energetic and is passionate about this subject.

Best marketing professor I encountered in Marshall, including core professor of course ;) 
Who is this class for? Anyone interested in marketing 
Final Thoughts: The class level is suitable for MBAs

career: Other | I am interested in Retail, CPG
comments:
Who is this class for? This class is ideal for students who want to move beyond basic marketing principles and develop a strategic, analytical mindset—especially those interested in tackling real-world business challenges, making data-driven decisions, and understanding how marketing fuels long-term growth in competitive markets.
Final Thoughts: I wish all Marshall professors could learn from Professor Silver’s approach to fostering a safe, inclusive participation environment. In many Marshall courses, class discussion is a significant part of the grade—but it can often feel intimidating to contribute. Professor Silver creates a space where students feel comfortable sharing ideas, whether ‘right’ or ‘wrong,’ which ultimately enhances learning for the entire class. More instructors should adopt this mindset!

One of the best classes I have ever taken in my academic career. Professor Silver does an excellent job of equipping you with a toolkit that you can apply to any Marketing Strategy situation you may find yourself in. The class has a $75 license and a course reader you must purchase. 

The license is for a simulation (StratX MarkStrat), which I think is one of the best simulations I have used. It will give you the opportunity to cut your teeth into data interpretation, and give you a nice risk free way to practice the things you learn in class.

This is hands down the best course I've taken at Marshall and Ike Silver is arguably the best professor I've had. It is not a difficult course at all but you will get a lot out of it. If you are interested in working in marketing, this course should be 100% mandatory in my opinion, but even if you're going into another field, you will definitely find value in this course. Ike is a very smart and articulate young professor and has a great sense of humor (the course is very entertaining). Part of the class in an on-going computer simulation that is pretty fun, and the rest is just a handful of cases and a bunch of very engaging lectures.

Easily the best elective I've taken so far. Silver keeps lectures interesting and applicable to almost all fields marketing or not. Midterm, final, and a semester long group simulation activity make up majority of the grade.

Workload consists of reading cases prior to discussion, submitting decisions for the marketing simulation, which is completed as part of a group, and studying for exam. Ike Silver makes the class very engaging and memorable.
Very manageable workload and is actually engaging, fun and dynamic class setting and teaching style, best suited for careers in marketing, consulting, sales, growth, strategy.

Workload is extremely easy! A few cases, markstrat decisions, midterm and final exam. Ike is a great engaging and fun professor. 10/10 would recommend this class for those who are interested in a career in marketing.

Fantastic professor with great energy. The content itself always runs risk of being dry, but Ike finds ways to make marketing strategy both engaging and intuitive. A fun course to get you to think about things from consumer perspectives. NOTE: you do have to purchase a license to run a simulation as part of the class.
Great class. Ike is engaging and makes the class very interesting. 5/5 highly recommend, especially for those planning on working in CPG marketing.

Professor Silver is a great professor and I would take any class he teaches. He is easily one of the most engaging professors at Marshall. He is young and a well respected researcher in his field of study.

Ike is a very engaging professor, he LOVES what he teaches and he is very current in research. I enjoy every class as we learn so much about human perceptions shaping purchasing decisions. It is super interesting for those into human psychology!
Ike is a great professor. Connects real life examples to class concepts that show how useful the material is. The marketstrat sim is also a great application of what we learn in class
Engaging and fun class with lots to learn.
Ike is a really good professor, super passionate and knows his content well. Very structured with his slides and presentation. Pretty light workload and easy tests.
Teaching style is fun, professor is super sweet and nice

This class is much more academic than it is preparing someone for a career in entertainment marketing. We cover very broad topics like what is humor and how does fashion play a role in our collective consciousness? If these are things you want to study, I recommend but I felt like this wasn't my goal from the class so I didn't get a lot out of it. I will say the professor did bring in some great guest speakers and that was the highlight of the class.
topic_title: MKT 561 - Strategic Marketing in the Creative Industries

comments: This class looks much more closely at what is creativity instead of how you can apply it to marketing. While the class is relatively straightforward, it was frustrating that we didn't get beyond talking about what humor was and how can you apply it to basic ads. The guest speakers, however, are very good.
topic_title: MKT 561 - Strategic Marketing in the Creative Industries

comments: Excellent guest speakers and nice professor. That said, the course is a little too involved with the theory behind marketing practices in the industry rather than application.
topic_title: MKT 561 - Strategic Marketing in the Creative Industries

comments: Only a few guest speakers were decent, everyone else was meh. You can find better guest speakers in other classes. It's mostly theoretical based and some things that are just common knowledge or sense. For example, we did a class on storytelling and he walked us through the three act storyteylling model, which to me could've been 5 minutes. I don't think I actually learned much in the class, so it's boring. However, the work is decently light. So if you want a class where you just talk about/listen to entertainment topics and have little work then sure, but don't expect to learn anything useful.

comments: Prof Schorr is very nice and loves the subject. He has great experience and many samples to bring to class! He is a bit funky but very sweet. Some of the frameworks overlap with International Strategy which is good reinforcement. Internationally focused students will love this class

This class definitely opens up my mind to other areas and gets me out of my comfort zone in order to foster creativity.

This is not the typical class. This class provides frameworks on dealing with stress, personal and professional roadblocks, and fears. You will have to write a lot of small deliverables and that may be annoying to some. You will have accept that you might be vulnerable or encounter other people's vulnerability to fully appreciate the class.

This class is fantastic. I haven't been put outside of my comfort zone like this in a class before, and I enjoy the assignments we have to do. Course is definitely achieving my stated goal of approaching life more creatively.

I enjoy this class a lot, but this class is not for everyone. I take it Thursday afternoons, and it's such a relaxing, thoughtful way to enter into my weekend.

"This class does not provide me with hard skills that I can use in a career in finance, but that wasn't why I took it. I have learned alot about my classmates and have gotten closer to them while at the same time learning about myself. This class is not for everyone, but if you are interested in taking a class that will help to better you personally (not solely professionally), then this may be a good class for you. To get the most out of it, you have to put a lot into it."

This class is truly a unique creature within an MBA curriculum. This class will challenge you, push you to consider how you interact with your life and others, and will get you outside your comfort zone. That being said, you also have to be receptive to what this class has to offer. From my perspective this is a "you get out what you put in" kind of class. Overall, I feel so lucky to get to take this class at business school and would recommend to anyone with an open mind who is willing to be vulnerable and try new things in the pursuit of their own growth and development.

FAIR WARNING - the class is half creativity and half group therapy. Therapy is great and it's great that people enjoy it... but I was hoping to have my creativity fostered. Hearing about the intimate pains of classmates honestly makes me uncomfortable. It's too much information. Doing the creative activities has been fun, but I would not take this class if I could do it over.

I highly recommend this class for anyone who struggles with ambiguity, identifies themselves as "not creative," and wants to be challenged out of their comfort zone. The class will push you to try new activities, and to become vulnerable with your peers in a way that most classes here in business school do not. It is up to you to be okay with the unstructured method, understanding that this class is for those who want long-term ROI and are willing to see the pay off once the class is done.

The class is less about "creativity" as an abstract concept and more about removing the barriers within yourself to become a more creative person. That said, you have to be down for the ride Joe is going to take you on. You need to embrace the concepts, try them out in your own life, and then share your experience with the whole class, something that can make people slightly uncomfortable.

*Sigh* I was really excited for this class because it was pitched as being unlike anything else you'd take at business school. What it ended up being was an off-brand weekly group therapy session run by someone who read a self-help book once. While I sympathize that this class was originally designed to be in person, Joe was COMPLETELY unprepared for the online environment and is incredibly disorganized. It feels like he kind of gave up when he realized it would be over Zoom and didn't adapt the material. He also has you pay a very expensive "lab fee" sight-unseen (which we have yet to see why it was that much) so buyer beware. 
The bright spots of the class are actually when he brings in guest lecturers to teach, which have been the most enriching parts of the class so far.
Good class if you care about mindfulness. You practice letting go of suffering, handling your inner critic, meditation, and getting out of your comfort zone.

This class is not difficult with regards to work-load (there are weekly reflective assignments) BUT only take it if you're willing to be open and share sometimes personal insights with the class. Great environment to get to know your peers better, learn about yourself, and become more mindful. As a consultant, the materials are also useful to learn how to motivate teams and create an environment where people are able to be creative.

So - there are some good nuggets here, but you can get those in any decent self-help book or podcast (or more individualized through weekly therapy). And I realize that these sessions are more suited for an in-person environment, but this "class" is so frustrating. The professor has been inconsiderate to students' needs while being incredibly unorganized himself, failing to set up basic resources for students like regular links for zoom and assignment submission on blackboard. This class involves a lot of personal sharing and feelings, which is OK, but he makes everyone speak every session and it feels kinda forced and a waste of time. Also still not sure what this has to do with creativity. That said, if you're trying to load your schedule with low-effort classes, this fits the bill, but I'd still try to something a little more useful like Influence or Negotiations.

This class feels a bit like a pyramid or MLM scheme in the sense that the professor promotes the idea of "embracing discomfort" and "mindfulness" to get away with not providing a good product. As someone mentioned above, he also requires an expensive "lab fee" so you literally have to buy in to it. However, if you are looking for something that isn't a ton of work to offset a more quantitative class schedule, this is it.

different kind of mba class. not a ton of work and you get to go on field trips. get what you put in
