A perfect way to practice and get out of your comfort zone in a completely safe enviornment. Not too much work and just about the value you gain. Also a great way to interact with classmates.
Negotiations is a skill you can use your whole life - a very useful class.

This is one of the best classes I've taken at Marshall! Professor Tost is super engaging. Workload is light and class is almost always shorter than 3 hours (usually around 2 hours). I was extremely uncomfortable with the idea of negotiating before this class, but every week has been fun and low stress.

One of the best classes I've taken, period. Even online, Professor Tost is super energic and engaging. She uses class time well, rarely using the full 3-hour sessions, and the in-class exercises reinforce key concepts. Very high reward/effort ratio.

Super great class. In terms of effort to put in for lessons learned, this is the best class I have taken at Marshall. Obviously it is more of a soft-skills based class, but still great. Would definitely recommend.

The Prof is excellent. She actually cares and is always open to feedback. This class is pretty much a core class - as almost everyone ends up taking it sooner or later. It teach important skills that are helpful in a lot of different situations. 3 different class sessions focus on Job Negotiations, Car Prchases and Home Buying - 3 very important negotiations in everyone's life.
Yes
Class is pretty chill but seriousness of the negotiations depend on who you're partnered with.

This is a course you can learn from an afternoon of reading the course book, after that it should be self explanatory. The good part of this class is that there are structured negotations that you do with a partner, so it provides negotiation practice. The teach is super nice, but there is a lot of course work with this professor. The nice thing is all of the content is in her slides (so you don't really need to buy or read the book), so all the assignments and tests should be a breeze

She has so much detail in her slides you don't need to buy the books (she even said don't worry about it because her slides cover everything) but because she is so detailed in slides there isn't time to ask questions during the lecture otherwise you won't get a break in the class. The practice negotiations are good but it isn't a must take class in my opinion.

I really like Christine. She is organized, friendly, and really cares about her students. She teaches mainly from the assigned books, but why reinvent the wheel if the method works. The structured negotiations drive home the key points and have helped me become more assertive, even if I anticipate rarely engaging in traditional negotiations.

I really like Christine. She is organized, friendly, and really cares about her students. She teaches mostly from the assigned books, but why reinvent the wheel if the method works. The structured negotations drive home the key points and have helped me become more assertive, even if I rarerly do a traditional negiation.

Professor is passionate and extremely organized, but the majority of the concepts are not really revolutionary. Negotiation simulations are fun. Workload is pretty light, although the final project paper seems to be a bit lengthy.

Lectures and course materials are useless, you can just read the slides after the fact. Prof is super nice but her energy is a lot to take sometimes. Negotiation simulations are kind of useful but so specific they're not must haves to be a better negotiator.
Professor is really nice. You don't have to read the material because lecture will cover everything from the book.
I love this class and I love Scott. Everyone should take Negotiations at some point during their time at Marshall.

Fantastic class with great hands-on experiences. Being able to practice different techniques we learn about in class is a great experience and I would highly recommend this class as a must-take in the MBA

Great class - a nice break from the normal class structure.  Lots of reading (that you don;t have to do to be successful) and otherwise reasonable work level and provides practical tools regardless of your next role.

This is an enjoyable class that is relevant both in your career and your personal life (i.e., negotiating business partnerships, but also negotiating things like the purchase of a car); the principles apply even outside of class. The first half of each session is spent in lecture, the second half you practice a "mock" negotiation. I found the practice negotiations very useful, they are complex enough that they feel relevant to real life and it helps build your confidence. The lecture piece, however, was dull. Prof. El Haddad pretty much just summarized the readings in bullet point slides. If you read the two main books on the syllabus "Getting to Yes" and "Negotiating Genius" you are getting the same concent that you will get from the lecture. So my take on this class is that the only valuable thing is the practice negotiations and related reflections. The concepts are not hard to grasp, just hard to put into practice, so for the everyday person your time is better spent just reading those two books in your personal time. BUT if you want an easy, enjoyable class that helps you build your confidence with being a negoiator, then this class is worth your time and Prof. Christine is friendly, fair, and provides good structure to her class.
Who is this class for? Should be relevant to all MBA students
Scott is great! He is very chill class is super easy but this class u have to go. and you'll get good grade if u show effort. I highly recommend improv class with Scott.

I like this class because it forces you to practice negotiation and negotiation skills that are taught during the course. The professor is quirky but she seeks to understand and work with you for the best. I don't really like how there are written midterms/final exams, especially since this class is social-based, but it's not the end of the world.
Love this class! Every session is a lecture and a real negotiation practice. Passionate professor and great experiences, highly recommend!
This class pushes you to step out of your comfort zone with being uncomfortable. Professor El-Haddad is amazing!
I think this class could easily be taught through a 1.5unit component. Christine is a kind professor, but a full blown semester is not needed to negotiate in my opinion.

Great class, everyone should take it. Skills are immediately useful. You do a practice negotiation in each class which is a nice way to balance the lectures. Prof is very precise and it can seem like an overly academic approach to a real-world skill, but that's being nitpicky.
It's a good class and interesting topics but midterm was a bit too intensive imo, and the in-class negotiations are a tad too "fake" for me to get much out of it from a practical perspective

This class teaches you the basics of negotiation tactics and deal-making. The first half of class is lecture and the second half is a negotiation. Light workload but the midterm has a lot of weight and is tricky.
Who is this class for? Helpful for all students to understand principles of negotiations
Professor is super nice and concepts are super applicable. Highly recommend
You get out what you put in, take the negotiations seriously.

Coursework is perfect. Professor is very sweet but she reads a lot from her slides. Given that she has put so much effort into building those slides, just using her slides to understand everything is sufficient
Course material is applicable for all parts of life - job negotiation, leasing an apartment, hiring a service, etc. Professor is fair and teaches well.

Total fluff class. Time is predominantly spent in breakout discussions where the professor allots way more time than necessary. No need to read any of the assigned readings because they're never referenced in lecture and they're pretty common sense. The group assignments are a waste of time (write a paper about a team that failed, write a paper about a team that succeeded). Had higher hopes to get more out of this class.
Lightest workload imaginable. Paying for credits

Tolan has a tendency to treat the class like an elementary school class - everything is extremely slow and she is a stickler for taking attendance and having cameras on if you want to Zoom (you also have to email her in advance if you want to Zoom into class). The workload is pretty minimal, but there are a lot of other classes that you can take if you want true classroom value. Feel free to take this class if you want an easier class/easier last semester.
This class is useless. We watched 45 minutes of a Bugs Life at one point. Take if you want ultimate fluff.

Absolutely a waste of time. This professor takes herself way too seriously and rubs students the wrong way. You'll watch bugs life in class and play with legos for 3 hours. Her assignment instructions sometimes are 2-3 pages long for a 1 page assignment. The guest speakers are not good. I'm sure there's good things to learn from the materials but it's hard to get over how the professor leads the class discussions. I'd avoid this class if you like to spend your money wisely.

Incredibly easy class that is full of personality quizzes and overcomplicated but easy assignments. Only take if you want a very chill class with friends but do not take if you really want to learn about leadership.

This is a good "senioritis" class, the workload is super manageable (5 page paper for a 6 person team!) and a good class to take with friends looking for a fun blowoff class. But you will not learn anything at all. The lectures are boring and not very fruitful, and the guest speakers are hit or miss. Sometimes it feels like the professor treats her students like kindergarteners, which can get annoying. If you are looking for a more meaningful class experience and want to make use of your tuition dollars, I would not recommend taking this class. Take literally anything else instead.
Horrible Class/worst class I've taken, waste of time and tuition, it's an easy class with lots of busy work but I haven't learned anything useful from this class

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. This is a complete waste of time. You can accomplish more in life by literally filling buckets of ocean water and immediately pouring them back into the ocean. This is not a good "senioritis" class; this is an absolute waste of time and there are better "fluff" classes where you will actually learn something. I actively lost brain cells sitting through this class and I'd rather be pounding sand. In that sense, this class is extremely difficult and the hardest class I've taken at Marshall because it is incredibly trying for my patience and silly. It's so hard to keep a straight face and take this class seriously because of how silly and half-baked the content is. Everyone hates this class and actively memes and jokes about it. I'd be willing to bet money to find one person who says anything positive about this class. The final project is a complete joke and completely ridiculous. If I took the concepts that this person is trying to "teach" into the real world, I would get laughed out of my job. This job teaches the opposite of leadership and I'd rather spend my time doing something productive, such as breathing, eating, sleeping, and most importantly, making money. Literally take ANYTHING else. Seriously, why is this class even a graduate course? This class would be good for undergraduates, but subpar even at that. Why is playing with legos or watching Bugs Life even relevant to anything? There is an exercise where we went through some "team contract" and watched the recording as well as "feedback" from another group. It was a complete joke and people treated it as such. Another class session was one of listening to some lady explain how to work on virtual teams. Anyone who lived through the past 4 years knows how to work on a virtual team, let alone a team. This class is for those with no work experience, perhaps a high school course? The professor also has misplaced priorities and does not build a good reputation with students. Worst class I've ever at Marshall and I'm generally very easy-going when it comes to feedback, but this is the one class I will die on a hill to provide negative feedback for.

Absolute worst class I have taken at Marshall in addition to the least likable professor I have encountered at USC. The class experience is absolutely painful, and includes a ton of busy work. The professor doesn't understand the group dynamics in elective classes and repeats exercises that were already done during orientation with core teams. The essence of the course material for this class is "be nice to your colleagues". Save your money and take literally any other class.

Boring class. There's a ton of reading and busy work, but you can get through the class without doing the readings. Professor is chill, but you will not learn any new valuable skills. Only take if you are looking for an easy elective and use time to work on other stuff. No quizzes or tests.

Who is this class for? Course is best for those still wary of working in teams or people who want to expand their ability to analyze teams
Final Thoughts: Class was fine. Was fun to work in groups but class was long and many lessons felt redundant and boring.

Jody Tolan is a high school level teacher attempting to teach graduate level students. 
Who is this class for? Ones who don't value their time.
Final Thoughts: It will make you worse.
Honestly, I had really high expectations for this class but was let down in every way. No direction or clear learning objectives. I don't 3 if Richmond is staying on board.
very good about leadership traits in business turnaround

Had high 3ations from previous class when i took this course, but didn't realize that the professor was changed for our year. Some guest speakers are interesting, but people spend most of his class finishing up with their emails. If you want a fluff course, yes this is perfect. But if you're looking to really get something out of that tuition money, i would advise not to.
First time this teacher is teaching this class. The class has GREAT potential and good cases...but the professor is NOT good. He ruins it.

This class has some amazing speakers. It is all soft skills, but I think the content is really valuable and the learnings will probably resonate way beyond business school. McCall is also a really good guy and insightful.

Had high hopes for this class but it didn't deliver. Prof is teaching the class for the first time and I found it hard to get any learnings from it. Brought in a few good guest speakers though and the project was useful.
Unfortunately, this class was absolutely useless.
The professor of the class seems knowledgeable and engaging but the class content is very fluffy and the syllabus lacks a coherent structure.

Prof. Richmond does not know how to teach any class, let alone an MBA level class. He is a terrible representation of Marshall and this class is completely worthless. You will not learn anything about leadership or executive development. You will read a lot of cases and watch your classmates present the same case discussion 3x per class. 4 avoiding this class until the professor changes.

"New professor to this course and has a lot of room for improvement.

Do you want to take the time to heavily engage and shape this course to make it worth while? Then go for it but I don't know of many MBAs with time to spare.

Do you need something a little softer to balance your otherwise intense schedule? This might be for you, too.

BUT do not just sit on your laptop the whole class. That would be a waste of time and tuition."

"If you like to pay for time to answer emails, check Facebook and finish up work for other class, this is the class for you! 

In all seriousness, this class is a mess. There is little organization or planning and, therefore, little motivation to take it seriously. The first couple classes were lessons mixed with cases mixed with commentary on disconnected YouTube clips and now it's just cases. I DO feel the professor is improving and this could be a great class going forward. He really is a great guy, it just seems this isn't his top priority. 

Though it could be strong in the future, as it stands now it is a waste of time and truly the most disappointing class I have taken at Marshall. 
"

This class is a lot of student discussion and the teacher talks about a lot of things that don't seem to be related to the course. Not the worst class, but I am confused about what we are supposed to be learning. Decent guest speakers though
Easy class, but you feel that you are not learning.

This is a must-take for any MBA.
This class completely turned my views around on how relationships (personal and professional) work.
There are many preconceptions you probably have not uncovered about workplace dynamics and relationship building, and this class will 'reveal' those to you, through fun role playing games, great readings and discussions, and class-A guest speakers.
This class energized me every Wednesday night and gave me a new perspective on life.

This class is extremely fluffy.
Some good speakers. Do not recommend unless you want to fit it into your schedule, or waste your tuition dollars.
The cases and projects are extremely useful. I find that the professor talks about concepts that diverge from the class - specifically he talks about the military, VR, and technology.
This course was exactly what I wanted: fluff with some slight application to my future.

This course is primarily taught looking at leadership development and organizational changes that occur with leadership changes.   The course is primarily focused on C-suite changes.  2nd half of the course, the professor brings in guest speakers.
Professor Bresnahan incorporates exercises and activities to lecture that make the class more interesting. The class is not very structured, so it's best to just go with the flow.

I really enjoyed learning about the leadership topics in Bresnahan's class. This is definitely a class that you will take out what you put in, as there are not many deliverables, and no exams. You can get by without putting much into it, however there is a lot to get out of it if you do the readings and engage in class.

This is not the most useful class but the discussion is absolutely top-notch and Bresnahan is an excellent moderator in terms of keeping the discussion on-topic and valuable. Chris is also an amazing person to know and is extremely knowledgeable in his area of focus. That said, I struggle to recollect exactly what I learned in this class. You are not likely to learn 'skills' that you can put into practice as you may with other classes, but hopefully you should get a broader understanding of how to be an effective leader and communicator in the workplace. Another flaw is that the learning tends to be targeted towards upper level leadership roles which most of us won't have access to until a few years out of school at least.

Overall I highly recommend this class as it's easy to do well if you just do the assignments, class conversation is very entertaining, and you get to know your classmates much better through their contributions to the discussion.

Lots of case and article readings, although they were interesting to read. Course consists of a lot of case discussion and discussion within your peers during class. In class discussion amongst peers make it more interactive, but really depends on your classmates if you want a meaningful discussion about actual course content.
 
 Course content is beneficial to learn about in theory - it really takes real life experiences on the job to really execute or realize what is discussed. Regardless it is useful to learn.

Interesting class, topics, and readings. We do a lot of self-assessments, which I love! Discussions are aways fun and engaging. Light in terms of assignments as well. If you want to build your soft skills, take it! I also think it's a good combo taking this class and the Power one.

The cases and discussions presented are essential to build leadership skills. Some concepts are not common sense, so you'll learn very useful things. Professor Bresnahan is funny, easygoing and bring a lot of real experiences to class.
This class is OK. Prof is engaging but we spend too much time taking self-evaluations. Light workload and no final, so it provides good balance if you have an otherwise rigorous load.
Great professor and some interesting content. Much of the course is group discussion based. A good course to pair with Interpersonal Power and Influence (MOR-567). Some interesting guest speakers.

Very unorganized - super behind on the syllabus with lots of readings that we never even discuss. Also, we were supposed to have guest speakers, which never happened. Great if you want an easy class where you fill out lots of self assessments. If you want to actually learn and develop as a person, this class is a waste of time.
Great professor and interesting assessments but doesn't work so well over zoom (discussion heavy and everyone is checked out)

We're so behind on the syllabus, which is fine if you don't have the time to do all of the readings. A huge miss on the guest speakers, although the one we had was great. There are a ton of discussion breakout rooms and self assessment, which end with a lot of silence since people aren't really focused on the class. If you're loking for an easy class, this is great. If you're looking to learn something groundbreaking, not so much.

Only take this class if you have not taken similar other classes. I took it to fill out my schedule but had already taken Interpersonal Power and the material is very similar. If I hadn't already taken that, I would perhaps find it more useful

Course couls have been useful, but the Professor ruined it for me. He didn't exhibit good leadership, he was outwardly biased, was unorganized, and didn't seem to care about the development of his students. Hard to take leadership advice from someone you don't respect as a leader.
Interesting class and the guest speakers were good. Lectures themselves weren't that exciting.

I don't think I will remember anything from this class. Course reader cost $200 and we have only discussed one reading in two months. You will get more out of Ken Perlman's Designing High Performing Organizations class.

Great guest speakers. Not much content to be learned but more from reflecting on yourself, but even that isn't done at much depth during the in-class discussions. Speakers are great though. Workload is light and done in a group of your own choosing.
Professor is nice and encourages good discussion.  Brings in guest speakers which helps keep things interesting.  Work isn't super stressful.

Light workload. You get out of this class what you put in as it is primarily reflection based. The basis in psychology research is interesting, but you need to think about how it applies to yourself to get much from it. The readings don't get discussed in class which is frustrating, but can add extra examples for those who still read them on their own. Class is somewhat duplicative with other MOR classes, particularly Interpersonal Influence and Power. Guest speakers are a nice change.

This class is like all other Chris B classes, you do learn more about leadership but it is like all other Chris B classes. I would take influence and power if you want to choose, but a good filler class

Here's the thing about Bresnahan: He's taken the chill professor thing so far that he basically doesn't teach or do anything. His course pack is a disaster (poorly Xeroxed articles you can barely read despite being available online), he doesn't give feedback on projects, and it's almost all group work so he doesn't have to do much grading. If you need a low stress course from a low stress dude, this is it. You can learn if you put in the work, but there are other MOR courses that are much more rewarding.

Bresnahan is a great lecturer--funny, insightful, engaging--and the class/content is interesting if you're at all into the psychology of leadership. Not a difficult course, just an entertaining and engaging one!
Boring
Easy course, some interesting speakers, class engagement may determine how interesting the course is, key takeaways are definitely applicable, but might be obvious
course is easy, prof is great. learnings depends on your participation in the course
One of the best professors. Very good course content. Very practical suggestions for being a good leader. Stimulating class discussions.

It is a very real-life-aligned course and very practical. The course will teach about leadership development in the professional career. I strongly recommend it for those who want to improve their leadership skills.

You can make this class work for you if you put in the time on your own. Very little work. Some good discussion with classmates. If you're looking to actually gain something from a class like this (and not just an easy course), I'd recommend Fostering Creativity instead.

It's a class where you take a personality quiz every day, and then talk about the results. A lot of his content has been debunked as pseudo-science, given concerns with reproducibility of the studies. He doesn't cite his sources very often so hard to taken anything he says seriously. He is on his phone a lot in class. He is generally likable, but class feels like a huge waste of time.

My review for this class is going to be extremely similar to Bresnahan's other class, Leadership and Executive Development, with the exception that Self-management skews somewhat towards being more directly useful and slightly less entertaining overall.

This is not the most useful class but the discussion is absolutely top-notch and Bresnahan is an excellent moderator in terms of keeping the discussion on-topic and valuable. Chris is also an amazing person to know and is extremely knowledgeable in his area of focus. That said, I struggle to recollect exactly what I learned in this class. You are not likely to learn 'skills' that you can put into practice as you may with other classes, but hopefully you should get a broader understanding of how to be an effective leader and communicator in the workplace. 

Overall I highly recommend this class as it's easy to do well if you just do the assignments, class conversation is very entertaining, and you get to know your classmates much better through their contributions to the discussion. However, if you area deadset on getting the most bang for your academic buck, you may want to look elsewhere.

He is very knowledgeable, passionate, and engaging. You take a lot of "tests" in class to see your personality, level of grit, narcissism, happiness, etc. Get to know yourself a bit better and hear different perspectives of your classmates.

This class isn't a heavy lift.  But, if you take the time to do the readings, the optional assessments, and reflect on your personal and professional development, it is definitely a class to take.  Chris is funny, an overall great guy, but extremely gregarious - probably not a professor for everyone, but I adore him.
Class wasn't always the most interesting. Some interesting discussion topics.

This is the second half of the MLFP coursework. This semester we were able to apply what we learned to coach our teams and use the class to discuss any problems we may be facing with our teams. Professor Heino has been great and I have enjoyed learning from her.

This is the second half of the MLFP coursework. This semester we were able to apply what we learned to coach our teams and use the class to discuss any problems we may be facing with our teams. Professor Heino has been great and I have enjoyed learning from her.

This is the MLFP course which you need to apply to get in. Professor Heino was new to teaching it this year and I think its likely going to get better and better as she gets more comfortable. The class is similar to the core leadership course and has elements of the SAUP core course but in a smaller setting that allows for more dialogue. The quality of conversation really depends on who else in in the class with you. I have mixed feelings about this course since it feels so similar to other core courses but I think the potential is there and hopefully it keeps getting better.

Professor Heino does a good job of allowing student discussion and letting the students dictate how the class progresses. I have found the in-class discussions to be fruitful and am hopeful this skills I learn will help propell in my career.

This course is purely to prepare you for coaching a core team in the fall through the MLFP program (and ultimately, to prepare you to lead teams in the professional world). You get as much out of this class as you put in, and if you want to become a better leader, this is a prime opportunity at Marshall to do it.

As others have mentioned, you must apply to MLFP to get into this class. Professor Heino shares leadership materials and allows for discussions in small groups. It is P/NP so if you show up and show effort it will be a very valuable class.

As someone who wants to be a leader this is a great course thanks to my classmates. We have such honest conversations about difficult topics and I'll be able to apply learnings to my career. I like Becky as a person but think she missed the mark with this class. She simplifies things way too much for an MBA level leadership program.

First half is very theoretical and almost too rudimentary for MBA students. Class moves slowly and doesn't feel applicable to coaching MBA students but is more relevant to real world teams/situations. However, the value of the coaching experience and being in class with other like-minded students makes up for it.
The first half of the MLFP coursework is very theoretical. I think the main appeal of the program is the core team coaching experience during the second half of the coursework in the fall.

The class provides me a platform to reflect on my leadership and teamwork experience. It is a comfortable room to share your thoughts and be open to improve because everyone is very supportive. The professor is lovely.
The class is part of MLFP program and specifically useful to develop coaching skills. the class really values the learning experience for everyone, C/NC

Good for anyone who appreciated the leadership class during core or anyone who knows that they further along you get in your career the less time you will spend "doing" and the more you will spend "managing." Feels like a cross between a class and a club. Light workload, nice chance to mentor first years, and it's a full year so you really get to know your classmates in a way you don't in other classes. Tends to self-select: if you're into this stuff you're INTO it.

Lots of introspection and reflection essays.
Who is this class for? Every MBA should apply for this class.
Final Thoughts: Amazing class. The in-person practice of leadership techniques really helps solidify learning. The accountability group is among the best meetings I have had at Marshall.
Great for those who love self/group reflection and discussions.

comments: If you don't have a strong interest in sports or interested in a career in sports, I wouldn't recommend this class. It's largely a discussion class based on current events (articles) and long course reader pieces, with minimal lecturing. You can get away with not reading the longer stuff but you'll still be expected to contribute in class. We have 4 guest speakers who are high-ranking executives in the sports and live events industries. If you're interested in sports as a potential career, then this is essentially a must-take class. Keep in mind that the professor has a very dry sense of humor and can be so direct it may come off as harsh at times. He could be more clear with his directions and grading rubric and is quite opinionated, but he knows what he's talking about and has a ton of experience and connections. Make sure to leave your fandom at the door—he strictly wants to talk about business implications which is largely a good thing.

comments:
Professor with an incredible amount of experience consuling in the sports industry and connections - more so than any other professor I have had so far. You do not have to be a sports die-hard as, in fact, he really tries to drive home the things that underpin the industry (government relations, labor stability, media, etc.) - it is not really about winning/losing. For each class you read 3-5 articles and then come in and discuss. If you read, attend class, pay attention and take notes in class, you will do fine. There are two 20 question, closed book mult choice exams (not cumulative) that he intentionally makes tough and curves. There is also one group paper/project of your choice that acts in place of a traditional final exam. 
The professor has a dry, sarcastic sense of humor. I like it, but it may not be for everyone. As long as you don't get your feelings hurt easily and know that is just his approach, you will be fine.

comments: Nan and TJ are both super kind and incredibly enthusiastic about the course. I went into the class not knowing what to expect, but I am pleasantly surprised at how many topics we have covered that are relevant to so many other subjects that have been touched upon across the business school curriculum. Though the course focuses on emerging economies, there is also substantial discussion around emerging markets within developed countries, so much of the material is a lot more relevant than I initially thought (since I don't personally plan to go work for a business based in an emerging economy). The course has some aspects in common with our required Global Strategy class, but with very different points of emphasis based on the professors' interests. (Sampling of some topics covered so far: different forms of corporate governance, family ownership, dealing with political risk, the uses and impacts of AI, operating in relationship-based economies.) Assignments include 5 "debates" (where we turned in 1-2 pages of notes on a given topic), a group project, and a midterm and final. The assignments haven't been too challenging since the professors are very clear about the points that they want us to remember, and they are fairly casual about their expectations on deliverables, likely in part because this is a new course.

comments:
Lots of group discussions but no group projects, very laid back reflection assignments
Who is this class for? Anyone interested in a leadership class that is more personally introspective and less business-oriented

Eric genuinely cares about his students, and it really shows in how he runs the class. The course is on the lighter side in terms of workload, which is a nice break, but you still walk away learning useful, applicable skills. A lot of the class is built around simulations in a game-like format, which honestly made it pretty fun. Eric also brings in a bunch of custom tools he built himself using AI, so the whole experience feels fresh and modern. I'd definitely recommend this class if you're looking for something lightweight that still teaches you something valuable.
topic_title: MOR 599 - Special Topics: Adaptive Leadership: Navigating Complexity and Change

comments: This is a great class that is very discussion based and helpful topic to be thinking about actively. There is quite a bit of reading, but the class is only once a week so it's a good balance to have during a full semester. There aren't many busy work assignments.
topic_title: MOR 599 - Special Topics: Women in Leadership: Power, Perception and Possibility

comments: You take this class during two weekends, both on Saturdays and Sundays. Because the class lasts from 9am to 4pm, you become really tired. The lectures and guest lecturers were good, and class materials can be helpful if you want to learn about biopharmaceutical marketing. However, I think the exams were too hard, especially for people who do not have scientific backgrounds.

This course teaches the evolution and business dynamics of the video gaming industry from the perspective of marketing and publishing teams. We learn how to write high value Amazon-style one-page business summaries on diverse business
gaming topics and are building towards a professional-grade go-to market strategy through our group project. It is led by Steve Fowler, a highly experienced business leader in the video gaming industry (former Publishing lead for Blizzard's Hearthstone). He brings in high-profile industry speakers and is taking us to Scopely for a studio visit. The course is very much aligned with the quality and expectations of an Marshall MBA course.
topic_title: CMGT - 537 - The Industry, Science and Culture of Video Games

comments: This class is so easy and It's online. You have to write weekly blog posts, but It's a four unit class. There are two group projects and one final project about Hollywood, streaming, and exploring the global industry.

This is a great class for anyone targeting entertainment industry. The professor is super knowledgable and structured, breaking down the elusive craft of a producer to easy understandable parts. She also invites awesome guests, who share relevant experience
topic_title: CNTV 521 - The World of the Producer
CNTV 521 - The World of the Producer

comments: If you already have entertainment industry experience, this class will feel like a waste of time. Covers basics of producing, covering development, financing, distribution, the representation businesses, etc. If you don't have experience and want to learn about how a project is produced, probably worthwhile.
topic_title: CNTV 521 - The World of the Producer

comments: If you are wondering how the TV industry works, take this class. Solid guest speakers and the professor, Tony Etz, is a lit agent @ CAA and a boss. Taking this class almost made me decide to become an assistant and work my way up to becoming an agent but then I wised up. Seriously though, I learned a great deal in this class. One of the better SCA offerings.

Not a lot of work (1 group project, 1 final presentation, 1 book to read during the semester, stay up to date on headlines too)
Who is this class for? If you want to understand the TV business and the behind the scenes work that goes into selling shows.
Final Thoughts: Class is taught at CAA, one of the leading talent agencies. Opportunity to ask real questions to professional writers, producers, etc.
Great information on film financing and how movies are packaged.
topic_title: CNTV 523 - Feature Film Financing and the Studio System

comments: The class has a great potential of teaching students about the business of entertainment. However, the professor sticks to the habit of reading definitions of various terms from his notes rather thsn tapping into his experience in the industry and engaging the students with the subject matter in a more organic and informative way. If interested in film classes- take a different one.
topic_title: CNTV 523 - Feature Film Financing and the Studio System

comments: This class is very helpful, giving a broad overview of entertainment.  I wouldn't suggest it for folks who've worked in the industry, but for people who are trying to break into entertainment, it's a class worth your time.  The professor rambles and mainly focuses teaching around what will be on the midterm and exam, which feels transactional.
topic_title: CNTV 523 - Feature Film Financing and the Studio System

comments: Look, this is a lecture class. He's gonna tell you stories for three hours every week. Its entertaining at times, mind numbing at others. Having a background in entertianment, there wasn't a TON of new material for me - but if you're trying to satisfy the Ent Biz certificate, this class isn't a ton of work, nor is it very difficult, and you'll get some anecdotes, for whatever that's worth.
topic_title: CNTV 523 - Feature Film Financing and the Studio System

comments: Jeff is a nice guy who actually does have some real experience, but he has the capacity to get very sidetracked, often on something completely unrelated to the proposed topics at hand. He does attempt to keep the structure of the course organized with weekly outlines which cover some high level things that he lists down teh definitions and explanations of. Again, if you have no experience and are looking for a taste, this could be useful, but for anyone who knows more than nothing about film, this is probably not a great use of resources.
topic_title: CNTV 523 - Feature Film Financing and the Studio System

comments: This is the Hulu class. Also the best class offered at USC. I learned more in this class than any at Marshall (for what I want to go into) and it has shaped the path I wish to take post graduation. If you wish to learn anything about the entertainment industry, digital industry, video games or the future, take this class.
topic_title: CNTV 524 - Digital Technologies and the Entertainment Industry

comments: The guest speakers are on the whole amazing, although some talks are better than others (as is to be expected). The class focuses on the digital disruption in the media space, so it is very timely. The two who lead the class are great as well: one is a partner at Greycroft, the other is at Hulu. A bit light on the business fundamentals, as I'm sure that info is highly confidential, but overall an interesting class.
topic_title: CNTV 524 - Digital Technologies and the Entertainment Industry

comments: This is the "Hulu" class. Both professors were execs at Hulu, so they have amazing speakers they bring in to speak about various relevant entertainment topics (SVOD, Live Events, etc.)
topic_title: CNTV 524 - Digital Technologies and the Entertainment Industry

comments: Enjoyed learning all about AI and its impact on the entertainment industry. A lot of work so be prepared.
topic_title: CNTV 524 - Digital Technologies and the Entertainment Industry

comments: This class is entertaining and you get some great speakers. Professor isn't organized.
topic_title: CNTV 525 - Entertainment Marketing in Today's Digital Environment

comments: There may be some value in the guest speakers, but they are hit or miss. Professor seems to enjoy talking about how he was tangentially involved in one or another movie that we've heard of, and continues to name drop quite shamelessly. I suppose if you had zero experience or knowledge of media and entertainment that the class could be useful, but if you have any experience in the space, do not waste your time/energy/money here. Also, a large portion of the class are non-MBA students, many of whom have the tendency to dominate the discussion in a non-productive way.
topic_title: CNTV 525 - Entertainment Marketing in Today's Digital Environment

comments:
Do expect quite many group presentations in the course as this is a marketing class. Prof is well connected in the industry so quite a few guest speakers and very good insights from them. Prof is very caring and supportive and gives out constructive feedback after every presentation you do, so it is a rewarding process.
Who is this class for? Anyone interested in film and TV marketing 
Final Thoughts: One of the best classes I have taken in Marshall. A lot of learning and great achievement through groupwork.
topic_title: CNTV 525 - Entertainment Marketing in Today's Digital Environment

comments: Not a ton of work and interesting guest speakers but not super structured
topic_title: CNTV 562 - The Motion Picture Studio and How it Operates

comments:
Weekly in-class group exercise; little work otherwise.
Who is this class for? If you are interested in understanding business side of filmmaking, worth taking.
Final Thoughts: Occasional high-level guest speakers and Bob's experience make this class worthwhile, but he does like to hear himself talk a bit too much
topic_title: CNTV 562 - The Motion Picture Studio and How it Operates

comments: If you like entertainment, want an easy class, and like to hear stories about celebritites then take this class. If you want to learn something useful that you can apply to your career, then this class has nothing for you. Basically a mixed level class with grads and undergrads about the entertainment industry and how it works from a professional agent viewpoint.  It's good for people with zero experience in entertainment (paritcularly film / tv) but if you have any experience this class is really an intro class for undergrads.  (What's an agent? What's a manager? How does a film get money?) You do get to listen to a lot of funny stories about famous people, so if you like watching TMZ then this a great class for you.  It's also taught in the CAA offices so be prepared to drive over there once a week.

If you don't like this class, you shouldn't work in entertainment.  This is how Hollywood teaches people.  It builds relationships, gives incredible exposure to great guest speakers, and candidly, isn't a heavy lift.  I understand this class could be more substantive, but you will not find a better or more respected professor at SCA than Alan Berger, who is a legend and still works at CAA.

Chose this course for my Business of Entertainment Certificate to learn about the agencies, as the professor is a TV agent at CAA, and it turned out to be a total waste of time and money. No structure at all. He invites famous guests, but they just share their life stories, rarely relevant to the current events in the industry. At one session, the professor invited interns from CAA, who bragged about buying sandwiches for the celebs, at another a 70-years old writer/actor spend 20 min saying hi to students' moms over zoom. Lol, it's funny, but it costs you $8K+ and you learn nothing except anecdotes about celebrities
Interesting guest speakers but not a lot of substance to the class

This class is amazing!! Not a ton of work and I've learned so much. Alan Braun is an amazing professor and it's been eye-opening and fun to learn about entertainment from those working in the industry and take a class off-campus at CAA. 10/10 would recommend.

This class is fantastic. You get the chance to learn the game development process with professors specific to your discipline (marketing, production, etc.). The level of individual attention is great. Fantastic class for anyone interested in the gaming industry.

Prof. Jaime is a best seller in UX Design. She shares the content of her new book with the students, even though it has not been published yet. There are HW every week, and they guide you to idealize an app, do customer interviews, validate the value prop, and design the front end. Coding is not required for this class - I didn't even see a single line of code. However, it is A LOT of work. So, only take it if you are trully committed.
topic_title: DSCI 556 - User Experience Strategy and Design

comments: This is an awesome class! As a non-engineer, I was intimidated to take a course at Viterbi, but the only quant is on the HW, not the tests, so it's very manageable. If you are pursuing a career in energy or even just interested in the topic I highly recommend! I am learning so much, and Prof Sanders is passionate and very organized.

"Amazing professor who has outstanding credentials and is passionate about the topic. Perfect for anyone trying to get a primer in energy fundamentals, electricity, and the industry in general. Classes are very much lecture based, with a few homeworks, a group research project, and multiple choice exams. No hardcore engineering content. Good opportunity to enjoy a Viterbi class on the other side of campus, and meet students outside of the Marshall bubble."

This is the BEST class I have ever taken at Marshall (lol, it is at Viterbi). Professor Sanders is such an awesome professor - she's so knowledgable, organized, passionate, and her lectures are so interesting. She covers the entire energy mix (transportation, electricity, agriculture) with a focus on emissions and the environment, and weaves public policy and overall societal impacts into every class, including covering 2-3 news articles from the last day or two that tie into our course in each lecture.  There is a homework and a quiz each week (sometimes with readings - like Biden's climate plan, or New Yorker articles) but the work feels really releveant and interesting and never like busy work (plus she drops the lowest two quiz and homework grades, and no exams). Totally doable for a non-engineering background. Highly recommend for anyone interested in renewable energy and or climate change and the environment.

Kelly is a great professor and super passionate. Regular course work (weekly HW and Quizzes) but the actual course load is light. Just be ready to power-walk to Viterbi to get to class on time...
[useful field] Yes - if you are interested in sustainability or greentech. The class is a fairly non-technical survey of global (but very US-focused) energy generation and associated environmental impacts, and lots of focus on current events and issues. You don't need to be an engineer to take the class.
Very dry lectures, but an interesting overview of the nonprof/philanthropy space if you are looking for a high-level understanding.

Cook is the best. 25 years as CEO at a top global PR firm well connected super easy going. learn a ton on brand strategy (probably more than a marshall course) highly recommend especially coming from a comms/PR background
topic_title: PR537 - PR and Branding: Branding with Purpose

comments: True Real Estate 101. Few MBAs, mostly architects, urban planners, and others wanting to get real estate experience. Part of the curriculum for Real Estate Certificate. Good professor, slow pace class, Easy A for the Excel advanced folks. Great intro to other aspects and economics of real estate. Better than FBE 591
topic_title: RED 510 - Real Estate Practice and Principles

comments: Class is very broad about real estate development and covers topics that give an overview on residential development. Good for those without a real estate background, but not necessary for those who are familiar with it or come with industry.
topic_title: RED 510 - Real Estate Practice and Principles

comments: Very important course to take. Open discussion around various topics that may pose risk to a company. It may not be useful in the first job out of college, but will be very useful as you become a decision maker 5-10 years later.
topic_title: RISK 599 - Special Topics: Conduct, Culture and Ethics Risk Management Through Films

comments: Professor Jaconi's classes are always well thought out and interesting. Even though I have no interest in surplus line insurance as a career path, every class I learn very valuable insights into the way insurance runs the world. Great guest speakers, and assignments are not too burdensome. Prof. Jaconi is a great teacher!
topic_title: RISK 599 - Special Topics: Distressed, Unique, High-Capacity, and Emerging Risk Transfer

comments: The professor is very well connected, very helpful for networking

Low lift class. The professor wants everyone to learn and is happy as long as you try.
Who is this class for? Students interested in learning how a company manages risk. If you're interested in cool guest speakers, this class could be right for you.
Final Thoughts:

Learning about risks provides valuable knowledge for assessing potential future challenges. It’s fascinating to explore the different types of risks and understand how major corporations handle them. I strongly recommend this course, Professor Kiko Harvey is one of the best professors I’ve met at USC, an incredibly experienced and inspiring educator.
